operations.description: This API is used to create CA tags in batches.
This API is used to create tags in batches for a certificate.
This API is used to delete tags in batches for a CA.
This API is used to delete multiple tags for a certificate.
This API is used to query the number of CAs by tag.
This API is used to query the number of the certificates by tags.
This API is used to create a tag for a specific CA.
This API is used to create a tag for a certificate.
This API is used to apply for a certificate.

There are three methods to create CAs. - Creating a root CA: All mandatory parameters must be specified. - Creating a subordinate CA and activating the certificate: All mandatory parameters must be specified. - Creating a subordinate CA without activating it: The request body contains only **issuer_id**, **signature_algorithm**, or **validity**.
This API is used to create an OBS agency for PCA to access OBS buckets and update the CRL. > Your token must have the **secu_admin** role assigned.
Buy a CA

This API is used to issue a certificate with a CSR. The constraints are as follows: 1. The default parameters are as follows: - Default CA parameters: - **keyUsage**: can be set to **digitalSignature**, **keyCertSign**, or **cRLSign**. The parameters in the CSR are preferentially used. - **SignatureHashAlgorithm**: SHA384 - **PathLength**: 0 (customizable) - Private certificate parameters: - **keyUsage**: can be set to **digitalSignature keyAgreement**. The parameter in the CSR is preferentially used. - **SignatureHashAlgorithm**: SHA384 2. When **type** is set to **INTERMEDIATE_CA**, the created subordinate CA certificate has the following restrictions: - It does not use the CA quota. The certificate is not returned when the CA list is queried. - Only the following two APIs can be used to obtain the information: Obtaining certificate details: GET /v1/private-certificate-authorities/{ca_id} Exporting a certificate: POST /v1/private-certificate-authorities/{ca_id}/export **certificate_id** returned by this API indicates **ca_id** of the subordinate CA. - Cannot be used to issue a certificate. The key is kept by the user. 3. If **type** is set to **ENTITY_CERT**, the created private certificate has the following features: - It uses the private certificate quota. When the private certificate list is queried, the certificate is returned. - The usage of other private certificates is the same as that of other private certificates, except that the key information is not exported (the key information is kept by the user.). > Note: Use **\r\n** or **\n** to replace the newline characters to convert the CSR into a string. For details, see the example request. Note: The organization information, public key algorithm, and public key content of a certificate are included in the CSR file and cannot be obtained through APIs.
This API is used to delete a certificate.

This API is used to delete a CA as scheduled. The scheduled time range can be 7 to 30 days. > Only the CAs in the **Pending activation** or **Disabled** status can be deleted. If the CA certificate is in the **Pending activation** status, the CA certificate will be deleted immediately. Scheduled deletion is not supported.
This API is used to disable a private CA. > You can disable a certificate only when it is in the **Activated** or **Expired** state.
This API is used to disable a CRL of the current CA.
This API is used to enable a private CA. > Note: This operation is allowed only when the CA is in the **Disabled** status.
This API is used to enable a CRL of the current CA.

This API is used to export a certificate. - International algorithm - When you configure the compression pattern, there are two cases: - If **is_compressed** is set to **true**, a compressed file package is returned. The package name is in the format of *Certificate name*_*Lowercase letters of the type field*.**zip**, for example, **test_apache.zip**. - For certificates issued with system-generated CSRs - If **type** is set to **APACHE**, the compressed package contains three files: **server.key** (key file in PEM format), **chain.crt** (certificate chain in PEM format), and **server.crt** (certificate in PEM format). - If **type** is set to **IIS**, the compressed package contains two files: **keystorePass.txt** (keystore password) and **server.pfx** (PFX certificate. The certificate and certificate chain are contained in the same file). - If **type** is set to **NGINX**, the compressed package contains two files: **server.key** (key file in PEM format) and **server.crt** (content in PEM format. The certificate and certificate chain are contained in the same file). - If **type**is set to **TOMCAT**, the compressed package contains two files: **keystorePass.txt** (keystore password) and **server.jks** (JKX certificate. The certificate and certificate chain are contained in the same file). - If **type** is set to **OTHER**, the compressed package contains three files: **server.key** (key file in PEM format), **chain.pem** (certificate chain), and **server.pem** (certificate). - For certificates issued with an uploaded CSR: - If **type** is set to **APACHE**, **IIS**, or **TOMCAT**, the compressed package contains two files **chain.crt** for the certificate chain in PEM format and **server.crt** for the certificate content in PEM format. - If **type** is set to **NGINX**, the compressed package contains only certificate file **server.crt** in PEM format. - If **type** is set to **OTHER**, the compressed package contains two files **chain.pem** for the certificate chain in PEM format and **cert.pem** for the certificate content in PEM format. - If **is_compressed** is set to **false**, a certificate in JSON format is returned, including the following parameters: - For certificates issued with system-generated CSRs - If **type** is set to **APACHE**, **NGINX**, or ** OTHER**, the return parameters are as follows: - **certificate**: the certificate content in PEM format. - **certificate_chain**: the certificate chain in PEM format. - **private_key**: the private key of the certificate, in PEM format. If a password is set when the certificate is exported, the encrypted private key is returned. - If **type** is set to **IIS** or **TOMCAT**, no definition is specified currently. - For certificates issued with externally imported CSRs - If **type** is set to **APACHE**, **NGINX**, **IIS**, **TOMCAT**, or ** OTHER**, the return parameters are as follows: - **certificate**: certificate content, in PEM format - **certificate_chain**: certificate chain, in PEM format - SM series cryptographic algorithms - When selecting whether to compress and whether to use SM series cryptographic algorithms, the options are as follows: - If **is_compressed** and **is_sm_standard** are set to **true**, a compressed file package is returned. The package name is in the format of *Certificate name*_*Lowercase letters of the type field*.**zip**, for example, **test_apache.zip**. - For certificates issued with system-generated CSRs - If **type** is set to **APACHE**", "**IIS**", "**NGINX**", or "**TOMCAT**", it is not defined currently. - If **type** is set to "** OTHER**", the compressed package contains six files. - **chain.pem**: the certificate chain in PEM format - **signCert.key**: the signature certificate key file in PEM format. If a password is set when the certificate is exported, the encrypted private key is returned. - **signCert.pem**: the signed certificate in PEM format. - **encSm2EnvelopedKey.key**: SM2 digital envelope file for encrypted certificates in BASE64 encoding format.(GMT-0009) - **signedAndEnvelopedData.key**: SM2 signature digital envelope file for encrypted certificates in BASE64 encoding format.(GMT-0010) - **encCert.pem**: encryption certificate in PEM format. - For certificates issued with imported CSRs - If **type** is set to **APACHE**", "**IIS**", "**NGINX**", or "**TOMCAT**", it is not defined currently. - If **type** is set to "** OTHER**", the compressed package contains five files: - **chain.pem**: the certificate chain in PEM format. - **signCert.pem**: the signed certificate in PEM format. - **encSm2EnvelopedKey.key**: SM2 digital envelope file for encrypted certificates in BASE64 encoding format.(GMT-0009) - **signedAndEnvelopedData.key**: SM2 signature digital envelope file for encrypted certificates in BASE64 encoding format.(GMT-0010) - **encCert.pem**: encryption certificate in PEM format. - If **is_compressed** is set to **true** and **is_sm_standard** is set to **false**, a compressed file package is returned. The package name is in the format of *Certificate name*_*Lowercase letters of the type field*.**zip**, for example, **test_apache.zip**. - For certificates issued with system-generated CSRs - If **type** is set to **APACHE**", "**IIS**", "**NGINX**", or "**TOMCAT**", it is not defined currently. - If **type** is set to "** OTHER**", the compressed package contains five files. - **chain.pem**: the certificate chain in PEM format - **signCert.key**: the signature certificate key file in PEM format. If a password is set when the certificate is exported, the encrypted private key is returned. - **signCert.pem**: the signature certificate in PEM format. - **encCert.key**: Private key for the encrypted certificate in PEM format. If a password is set when the certificate is exported, the encrypted private key is returned. - **encCert.pem**: encrypted certificate in PEM format. - For certificates issued with uploaded CSRs - If **type** is set to **APACHE**", "**IIS**", "**NGINX**", or "**TOMCAT**", it is not defined currently. - If **type** is set to "** OTHER**", the compressed package contains four files: - **chain.pem**: the certificate chain in PEM format. - **signCert.pem**: the signature certificate in PEM format. - **encCert.key**: Private key for the encryption certificate in PEM format. - **encCert.pem**: encryption certificate in PEM format. - If **is_compressed** is set to **false** and **is_sm_standard** is set to **true**, a certificate in JSON format is returned, including the following parameters: - For certificates issued with system-generated CSRs - If **type** is set to **APACHE**, **IIS*, **NGINX**, or **TOMCAT**, it is not defined currently. - If **type** is set to ** **OTHER**, the following parameters are returned: - **certificate_chain**: the certificate chain in PEM format. - **certificate**: the signature certificate content in PEM format. - **private_key**: the private key of the certificate, in PEM format. If a password is set when the certificate is exported, the encrypted private key is returned. - **enc_certificate**: Encryption certificate content in PEM format. - **enc_sm2_enveloped_key**: SM2 digital envelope file for encrypted certificates in BASE64 encoding format.(GMT-0009) - **signed_and_enveloped_data**: SM2 signature digital envelope file for encrypted certificates in BASE64 encoding format.(GMT-0010) - For certificates issued with imported CSRs - If **type** is set to **APACHE**, **IIS*, **NGINX**, or **TOMCAT**, it is not defined currently. - If **type** is set to ** **OTHER**, the following parameters are returned: - **certificate_chain**: the certificate chain in PEM format. - **certificate**: the signature certificate content in PEM format. - **enc_certificate**: Encryption certificate content in PEM format. - **enc_sm2_enveloped_key**: SM2 digital envelope file for encrypted certificates in BASE64 encoding format.(GMT-0009) - **signed_and_enveloped_data**: SM2 signature digital envelope file for encrypted certificates in BASE64 encoding format.(GMT-0010) - If **is_compressed** is set to **false** and **is_sm_standard** is set to **false**, a certificate in JSON format is returned, including the following parameters: - For certificates issued with system-generated CSRs - If **type** is set to **APACHE**, **IIS*, **NGINX**, or **TOMCAT**, it is not defined currently. - If **type** is set to ** **OTHER**, the following parameters are returned: - **certificate_chain**: the certificate chain in PEM format. - **certificate**: the signature certificate content in PEM format. - **private_key**: the private key of the certificate, in PEM format. If a password is set when the certificate is exported, the encrypted private key is returned. - **enc_certificate**: Encryption certificate content in PEM format. - **enc_private_key**: Private key of the encryption certificate in PEM format. If a password is set when the certificate is exported, the encrypted private key is returned. - For certificates issued with imported CSRs - If **type** is set to **APACHE**, **IIS*, **NGINX**, or **TOMCAT**, it is not defined currently. - If **type** is set to ** **OTHER**, the following parameters are returned: - **certificate_chain**: the certificate chain in PEM format. - **certificate**: the signature certificate content in PEM format. - **enc_certificate**: Encryption certificate content in PEM format. - **enc_private_key**: Private key of the encryption certificate in PEM format. > Only certificates in the **Issued** status can be exported.
This API is used to export the CA certificate. > Note: You can export a certificate only when it is in the **Activated** or **Expired** state.
This API is used to export a Certificate Signing Request (CSR) of a CA. > A CSR can be exported only when the corresponding CA is in the **Pending activation** status.

This API is used to import a CA certificate. To use this API, the following conditions must be met: - (1) A subordinate CA must be in the "PENDING" state. - (2) The imported certificate body must meet the following requirements: - a. The certificate signing request must be exported from the PCA system when the certificate is issued. - b. The completed certificate chain must be imported if you need to export a complete certificate chain later. - c. The certificate body and chain must be in PEM format.
This API is used to activate a CA. > You can activate a certificate only when it is in the **Pending activation** status.
This API is used to query the CA list by tags.
This API is used to query the tag list for a CA by its certificate ID.
This API is used to query the certificate list by a specific tag.
This API is used to query the tag lists for a certificate by its certificate ID.
This API is used to query the private certificate list.
This API is used to query the CA list.

This API is used to query the list of OBS buckets. > This API can be used only when an agency is created. For details about how to create an agency, see **Certificate Revocation** > **Creating an Agency** in this document.
This API is used to query the list of tags configured for all CAs.
This API is used to query the list of tags configured for all certificates.
This API is used to parse a CSR.
This API is used to restore a CA status from **Schedule deletion** to **Disabled**. > Note: Only a CA in the **Pending deletion** status can be restored.
This API is used to revoke a certificate. > Note: If you do not want to provide the revocation reason, set the request body to **{}**. Otherwise, an error will be reported.
This API is used to revoke a subordinate CA. >If you do not want to provide the revocation reason, set the request body to **{}**. Otherwise, an error will be reported.
This API is used to query details about a certificate.
This API is used to query details about a CA.
This API is used to check whether you have the agency permission. > Your token must have the **secu_admin** role assigned.
